ITEM.PTXT: Driver and front passenger SRS airbags, a driver SRS knee airbag, seat belts with pretensioner + force limiter, SRS side airbags and SRS curtain shield airbags are provided on all models.
A communication and disposal processing function with a disposal tool has been provided for disposing of the airbags when scrapping the vehicle.

ENTRY.PTXT: When a strong impact that could seriously injure the occupants is received, the bag that acts as a cushion inflates instantly, working together with the restraining action of the seat belts to reduce the impact to the occupants' heads and chests.
Seat Belt with Pretensioner + Force Limiter
When a strong impact is received from the front of the vehicle, the pretensioner mechanism instantly retracts the seat belt to increase occupant restraint.
When a load above the specified value is applied to the seat belt, the force limiter mechanism maintains that specified value, reducing the impact applied to the chest.

MECA.TITLE: SRS Airbag & Seat Belt with Pretensioner System Operation

ITEM.PTXT: The SRS airbags & seat belts with pretensioner + force limiter operate when an impact above a certain level is detected in a frontal collision.
SRS airbag operation assumes a collision with a wall that does not deform or move, at a collision speed of approximately 25km/h or more, within a range of approximately 30° in front.

Because the front airbag sensors and the G sensor in the center airbag sensor (computer) detect deceleration during a collision, the airbags may deploy in situations in which a strong impact is received from underneath the vehicle. (When striking a curb, etc., when falling into or driving over a deep hole or ditch, when jumping and striking the ground, when falling off the road, etc.)

MECA.TITLE: Cases in Which the SRS Airbag & Seat Belt with Pretensioner System Does Not Operate

ITEM.PTXT: Because the front airbag sensors and the G sensor in the center airbag sensor (computer) detect the deceleration in a collision acting from the front of the vehicle, the airbag system may not operate depending on the situation. In addition, even in a frontal collision, the system does not operate if the deceleration does not reach the specified value of the sensors.

MECA.TITLE: SRS Side Airbag & SRS Curtain Shield Airbag System Operation

ITEM.PTXT: The SRS side airbags operate when the cabin body receives a strong impact from the side of the vehicle and the side airbag sensor and airbag sensor (computer) detect an impact above a certain level. The SRS curtain shield airbags operate when the cabin body receives a strong impact from the side of the vehicle and the side airbag sensor, rear airbag sensor and airbag sensor (computer) detect an impact above a certain level.

MECA.TITLE: Cases in Which the SRS Side Airbag & SRS Curtain Shield Airbag Do Not Operate

ITEM.PTXT: Even in a side collision, depending on the collision conditions, the collision energy may be reduced by deformation of the vehicle body and doors so that the ignition criteria of the sensors are not reached, and the SRS side airbags & SRS curtain shield airbags may not operate.

Ignition of the driver and front passenger airbags, driver knee airbag and pretensioners is determined from the signals from the front airbag sensors and the G sensor in the center airbag sensor (computer), and ignition of the SRS side airbags and SRS curtain shield airbags is determined from the signals from the side airbag sensors and rear side airbag sensors. In addition, it has a diagnosis function and performs self-diagnosis when a system malfunction occurs.

ITEM.PTXT: Communication with a disposal tool and a disposal function are provided for disposing of the airbags when the vehicle is scrapped.
A batch deployment connector is provided on the center airbag sensor (computer).
By connecting a special tool to this connector, batch deployment of the airbag system is possible.

An information label indicating the mounting location of the center airbag sensor (computer) is affixed above the front passenger door lock striker. For this vehicle, it indicates that the center airbag sensor (computer) is mounted on the floor tunnel at the front of the center console.

The airbag system is effective when the occupant is seated in the correct posture and wearing the seat belt correctly. Do not place objects or attach accessories, etc. near the deployment areas. Injury may occur when the airbag operates. In addition, if there are scratches or damage on the airbag deployment area, do not continue to use the vehicle and consult a dealer. For details on the SRS airbags, refer to the Owner's Manual.
Caution labels for users are affixed to the driver and front passenger sun visors.
The center airbag sensor (computer) consists of a G sensor, an ignition determination circuit, a backup power source, etc.

Based on the signals from the front airbag sensors and G sensor, it determines ignition of the driver and front passenger SRS airbags, driver SRS knee airbag and pretensioners, and based on the signals from the side airbag sensors and rear side airbag sensors, it determines ignition of the SRS side airbags and SRS curtain shield airbags. In addition, it has a diagnosis function and performs self-diagnosis when a system malfunction occurs.

ENTRY.PTXT: When deceleration is applied by an impact, it outputs a signal that is linear with respect to the deceleration.
Consists of a backup capacitor that supplies power to the system in a collision or if the power supply system fails, and a booster circuit that raises the voltage.

Performs specified calculations based on the signal from the front airbag sensors, and sends an ignition signal when the calculated value exceeds a preset value. In addition, the malfunction diagnosis circuit diagnoses whether there is a malfunction in the entire system and informs the driver of any system malfunction, and the diagnosis function diagnoses the location of the system malfunction.

ITEM.PTXT: The SRS airbags, driver SRS knee airbag and seat belts with pretensioners are ignited by the impact of a frontal collision. The determination is made based on the front airbag sensor signals and the signals from the G sensor and electronic safing sensor in the center airbag sensor (computer).
The SRS side airbag is ignited when both the side airbag sensor signal from a side impact and the electronic safing sensor in the center airbag sensor (computer) turn ON.

The SRS curtain shield airbag is ignited by the ignition signal of the SRS side airbag that satisfies the above conditions, or when both the rear side airbag sensor signal and the electronic safing sensor in the center airbag sensor (computer) turn ON.
To keep a record of deployment, the center airbag sensor (computer) keeps the SRS airbag warning light illuminated even after the primary check. This SRS airbag warning light cannot be cleared.
The operation of the diagnosis circuit is indicated by the SRS airbag warning light in the meter. The diagnosis circuit operates in 2 periods: the primary check and the constant check.

When the engine switch is turned to IG ON, the SRS airbag warning light illuminates for approximately 6 seconds and the primary check is performed. During this period, ignition is prohibited and the operation of the center airbag sensor is diagnosed. If a malfunction is detected during this primary check, the SRS airbag warning light remains illuminated and does not go off even after 6 seconds have elapsed.
For a center airbag sensor that has deployed the airbags, the SRS airbag warning light remains illuminated even after the primary check, regardless of whether there is a malfunction.

After the primary check is completed and the SRS airbag warning light goes off, the system enters the ignition-enabled state, and the diagnosis circuit constantly checks the system for malfunctions. If a malfunction is detected during this constant check, the SRS airbag warning light illuminates. (The warning indication for low power supply voltage goes off after the power supply voltage returns to normal.)

By switching to the diagnosis mode, the diagnosis result for the malfunction location can be displayed by the number of times the indicator light blinks. In addition, a new diagnosis function has been adopted, and the diagnostic trouble code for the malfunction location can be read by connecting a diagnostic tool to DLC3. For details on the diagnosis mode, refer to the Repair Manual.
A service caution label describing handling precautions, etc. is affixed to the top of the center airbag sensor (computer).
